newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks inch to higher close on heavy trade.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks inch to higher close on heavy trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks edged to a slightly higher close on Thursday, chiefly due to a more positive interest rate outlook and demand for local market leader HSBC Holdings, brokers said.
"We opened strong on the back of Wall Street," said Richard Verin, head of equities trading at CS First Boston. "Then we saw alot of switching during the remainder of the day."
The Hang Seng Index inched ahead 5.60 points to close at 13,416.36 after soaring to a high of 13,568.86 at the start of trade.
Trading activity was brisk throughout the day with turnover rising to a hefty HK$12.31 billion, well up on Wednesday's HK$10.73 billion.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 93.13 points to close at 6,945.85 on Wednesday, following comments by the U.S. Federal Reserve chief Alan Greenspan which eased fears of interest rate hikes.
Greenspan also said he thought the stock market was properly priced, if corporate earnings estimates were accurate.
Banking giant HSBC Holdings was the most actively traded issue, rising HK$2.50 to close at HK$190.50.
Hang Seng Bank closed down HK$0.50 to HK$83.00.
"The gap between the two (HSBC and Hang Seng Bank) is at its widest in the last year or more," said Verin.
China Eastern was the second most actively traded issue, putting on HK$0.16 to HK$1.87 on trade of HK$497.57 million.
Brokers said new broad-based retail interest in red chips was seen on Thursday.
H share Guangdong Kelon continued its bull run, putting on HK$0.10 to close at HK$7.35.
Profit-taking in the property counters, chiefly Cheung Kong, pulled the market down in late afternoon trade, brokers said.
Cheung Kong rose to a high of HK$76.75 on rumours that the sales prices of its latest luxury residential property was likely to be 30 percent higher than analysts had previously forecast.
The share closed HK$0.75 higher at HK$75.75.
The March contract closed 40 points higher at 13,440 and the April contract eked out a gain of 27 points to end at 13,435.
